channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Flemish People's Movement denounces lack of Dutch-language hospital care
item.description: A convoy of 25 cars and seven mopeds drove past three Brussels hospitals as campaigners claimed Dutch-speaking patients still lack proper emergency and general care.

item.title: 150 people arrested during Brussels riots
item.description: People threw projectiles at police officers and committed deliberate arson, among other things.

item.title: Two injured in Brussels café fire overnight
item.description: One of the victims had to be resuscitated on the way to the hospital.

item.title: Police stop antifascist protesters in Anderlecht but unrest continues
item.description: The protest that began in the morning hours progressed rapidly as police tried to confront the 500-strong crowd.

item.title: Antifascists gather at Brussels central station
item.description: Several hundred protesters got together to raise a voice against the police. Authorities searched several people in an attempt to curb their efforts.

item.title: Man arrested for murdering mother in Brussels home
item.description: The police started investigating after the kids were not picked up from school one day, and proceeded to find a dead body in the flat.

item.title: More than just drinks: Five Brussels cafés with unique concepts behind them
item.description: The Brussels Times selected five venues that go beyond the usual in trying to grasp visitors’ interest.

item.title: Iconic Brussels hotel named among 15 best in Northern Europe
item.description: The prestigious Brussels hotel has been recognised as one of the best hotels in Northern Europe in the Condé Nast Traveler Readers’ Choice Awards 2026.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 16 – 18 October
item.description: Do you want to turn the clock back to 1990 or explore unique pathways in the inner city? Luckily, you can do both and much more at events across Brussels this weekend.

item.title: 'Blatant failure': Brussels residents launch petition to change Schuman roundabout
item.description: Residents of Brussels’ European Quarter are calling for a rethink of the recently redeveloped Schuman roundabout, criticising its lack of greenery, shade and seating.

item.title: Brussels acquires monumental sculpture in Haren to expand public art collection
item.description: The City of Brussels has acquired a monumental artwork by Latvian artist Evita Vasiljeva in Haren.

item.title: 'Anything but superfluous': Brussels Minister-President doubles down on need for drug commissioner
item.description: The general prosecutor of Brussels, Frédéric Van Leeuw, called it "a laughable idea" to appoint a Brussels drug commisioner while a federal one is already in place

item.title: Archive and Museum of Flemish Life in Brussels opens archives on Museum Night
item.description: The Archive and Museum of Flemish Life in Brussels (AMVB) will exceptionally open its archive for guided tours on Saturday 17 October for Museum Night Fever.

item.title: ‘We will never forget you’: Brussels officer Nordine El Talbi mourned after fatal shooting
item.description: The officer who was killed in the line of duty on Monday evening has received an outpouring of support from colleagues, public officials and Belgian citizens alike.

item.title: European Schools continue 'unlawful' short-term contracts in Brussels despite court ruling
item.description: Every school year, some employees are left awaiting confirmation as to whether the school wishes to continue employing them or whether they will lose their jobs without any compensation.

item.title: 'Violence is undermining society': Brussels mayor asks for more police funds after shooting
item.description: "We knew there were going to be incidents. A very experienced police officer has been shot. People don’t realise that the violence is undermining society."

item.title: 'No women allowed': Amnesty International stages protest in Forest Park
item.description: The action was staged as a show of solidarity with Afghan women.

item.title: Over 5,000 students will cycle to school on Thursday as part of safety campaign
item.description: Students and staff members from 65 schools are expected to participate in the 'Be Bright' campaign.

item.title: Fatal shooting next to European Parliament on Monday night - perpetrators still at large
item.description: A man was shot and killed in an apartment block next to the European Parliament on Monday. The perpetrators are still at large according to the Brussels public prosecutor.

item.title: Police officer shot in head while investigating carjacked vehicle in Brussels, several held in custody
item.description: Officer Nordine belonged to the Anti-Aggression Brigade of the Brussels-Capital/Ixelles police zone, a unit deployed in particularly high-risk armed operations.
